title: AutoML-Agent: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Full-Pipeline AutoML

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4: 'we use GPT-4 (gpt-4o-2024-05-13) as the backbone model for all agents and LLM-based baselines'; App. B.3: 'gpt-4-2024-05-13 models via the OpenAI API'

prompt.location: Appendix B.3 'Zero-Shot Prompt for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 Baselines' + Table 3/4 user instructions + Appendix B.1 skeleton script
prompt.note: AutoML-Agent's own agent prompts are also printed, but its prompt agent is a LoRA-tuned Mixtral that is not released in the paper

claim.location: Table 6, row GPT-4, column Avg. (constraint-free); 14 datasets x 5 runs

data.source: 14 public datasets listed in Table 5 (Kaggle / HuggingFace / Time-Series-Library): Butterfly Image, Shopee-IET, Ecommerce Text, Cora, Citeseer, Weather, Electricity, etc.

notes: Claim chosen is the zero-shot GPT-4 baseline, not the headline AutoML-Agent SR=1.000 (needs the fine-tuned prompt agent and full multi-agent loop). SR requires executing each generated pipeline (training models on 14 datasets) in a runtime; API cost is low but compute/setup is heavy.

resolution.plan: SR is execution-based (Appendix: 0 = code fails, 0.5 = runnable model, 1.0 = runnable model plus a deployment endpoint), so the number needs a Python runtime with the 14 public datasets (Table 5 links) rather than the authors' code. For each dataset build the Appendix B.3 zero-shot prompt with the Table 3/4 user instruction, sample 5 completions from gpt-4o-2024-05-13, execute each returned pipeline in a fresh environment and grade on the 3-level scale; average over the 70 runs and compare with 0.314 (Table 6).
resolution.approximation: Runtime, package versions and dataset downloads (Kaggle) differ from the authors' environment; decoding parameters unstated.
